paragraphs: Touch typing is a lot like playing the piano. First your fingers learn scales: short, simple, repeated moves. Then the moves turn into words, and later into whole sentences. Do not rush. A steady rhythm and accuracy bring speed on their own.

Sit up straight and place your fingers on the home row. Your index fingers feel the small bumps on two keys. After every press the finger returns to its place. Your eyes stay on the screen while your hands remember the way.

The town is still asleep in the early morning. The streets are quiet, and only a cleaner sweeps leaves near the bus stop. Then the bakery opens, and the air smells of fresh bread. People hurry to work, and the new day picks up its pace.

You do not need a special talent to learn something new. You need patience and a short lesson every day. Twenty minutes of careful work give more than two hours of hurry. A mistake is not a problem: it shows what to repeat.

A small river runs across the meadow behind the village. In summer children fish there and swim until evening. In autumn fog hangs over the water, and in winter the river hides under the ice. Every season paints it in its own way.

A good letter starts with a greeting. Then the author explains in a few words why they are writing. One idea, one paragraph: it is easier for the reader. At the end, say thank you and sign your name. Read the text again before you send it.
